historical_references.reference: Ibn Manzur, Lisan Al-Arab. Niknam is an honorific title given to certain high-ranking officials in the Abbasid Caliphate. It is derived from the Arabic word nikamah, which means 'recompense' or 'reward'.

Al-Maqrizi, The History of Damascus. Niknam is a title given to the ruling family of Damascus during the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods. It is derived from the Arabic word nikamah, which means 'revenge' or 'forceful retaliation'.
